text:
jamie: quick q — proposal on the table: keep internal control plane gRPC/proto-first, and maintain a thin REST shim at the edge for external clients. where should routing policies, quotas, and token-level telemetry live?

rohan: proto-first makes life easier for contract evolution and streaming. :+1: but the shim will create duplicate surface area for quotas unless we centralize enforcement.

emily: important: billing/usage dashboards need token-level telemetry tied to model-version. if we push all quota enforcement to the gateway we risk losing accurate cost attribution. :thinking:

sasha: auth perspective: gateway should handle authentication (JWT/mTLS) and coarse tenant quotas. fine-grained per-model/version quota checks should be control-plane calls (cacheable). also prefer header-based hints: e.g., `X-Rdwd-Tenant` + `X-Rdwd-Request-Attrs`.

jamie: that matches my thinking. Gateway = fast gatekeepers (auth, basic rate limits, IP safelists). Control plane = policy decision point for routing (model variants, canary %, fallback rules) and quota accounting. for latency-sensitive fallbacks, we might allow gateway-local fast fallback options.

rohan: implementation nit: keep one canonical mapping artifact for shim -> grpc, not per-service copies. suggest `api-mapping.yaml` checked into platform repo and used for codegen + envoy config. example: 
```yaml
- rest: POST /v1/generate
  grpc: inference.Service.Generate
  transform: body.prompt -> request.prompt
  headers: [X-Rdwd-Tenant]
```

emily: +1 to single source of truth. telemetry needs hooks at both places: gateway for latency tails, control plane for token accounting and model signals. we can emit `trace_id` and `model_version` in spans so dashboards can join.

sasha: one more: fallback policy enum we should standardize: `fast_local`, `safe_control`, `disabled`. fast_local = gateway returns cached/KV fallback quickly; safe_control = ask control plane and potentially fall back to cheaper model variant; disabled = no fallback. policy should be attached to the route in mapping file.

jamie: agreed. owners? propose platform owns mapping + policy enforcement APIs; infra owns envoy integration; telemetry owns signals contract. action items:
- jamie: draft `api-mapping.yaml` schema + enum defs by EOD Fri
- rohan: spike server-side policy hook for proto stubs (2d)
- emily: list telemetry fields we need (token_count, model_version, route, trace_id)
- sasha: produce short threat model for gateway shims (1w)

infra-bot: deploy-check: mapping schema PR CI will run schema linter and integration tests.

devex-bot: note: will add example mapping + client snippet to quickstarts when schema lands.

rohan: cool. i'll start the stub spike tomorrow. thanks all! :rocket:
